Attack the same 73.8% scalar-panel bottleneck with a normal-equations path that is almost pure tensor-core GEMM: G = A^T A (batched cublas SYRK/GEMM), R = Cholesky(G) (custom batched CUDA C++ Cholesky or cuSOLVER potrfBatched), Q = A R^{-1} (batched TRSM), then reconstruct compact Householder (H,tau) from the orthonormal Q via the LAPACK orhr_col algorithm so output matches the geqrf contract exactly (watch the diagonal sign convention so householder_product(H,tau) reproduces Q). Robustness is the hard part and is gated: ill-conditioned rankdef/clustered/nearrank/mixed cases must be correct ON THEIR OWN MERITS (functional-invariance guard forbids content-dispatch). Use shifted CholeskyQR2/CholeskyQR3 with a breakdown fallback to Householder; FP32 factors out.

CholeskyQR3 + orhr_col (PyTorch). All 22 test shapes + invariance + off-grid guards PASS. diff_correctness guard flagged 1/8 inputs on b640-n512 cond2 (orth residual 0.00827 > allowed 0.0061): the _ORTH_TOL=1e-2 max-abs verify is looser than the checker's scaled-L1 orth test, so a borderline matrix slipped past instead of falling back to geqrf. Fix: tighten verify to match checker metric.

CholeskyQR3 + orhr_col, CORRECT: all 22 tests + differential + invariance + off-grid guards PASS. Fixed the verify (orthogonality scale uses ||I||_L1=1 not n; added factor-residual gate; forced FP32 matmul no TF32). Geomean 159468us, slower than baseline 111805us. Per-shape: well-cond b640-n512 cond2=266606us (fast path), but rankdef b640-n512=1170278us (full geqrf fallback) and n4096=588859us drag the geomean up. The PyTorch getrfnp Python loop (~950ms standalone for b640) is the dominant fast-path cost. Next: custom CUDA getrfnp kernel + cheaper fallback.

Custom CUDA getrfnp panel kernel (one CTA/matrix, coalesced row-parallel rank-1 update) + batched-GEMM trailing update for the orhr_col reconstruction; verify runs before reconstruction so fallback matrices skip getrfnp. Geomean 78293us vs baseline 111776us = 1.43x. All 22 tests + differential + invariance + off-grid guards PASS. Per-shape: b640-n512 dense 5.1x, clustered 5.4x, n176/n352 ~5x; losses on b8-n2048 (0.39x), b2-n4096 (0.16x, 100% fallback), rankdef b640-n512 (0.88x, 100% fallback), nearrank n1024 (0.76x). Next: cheaper getrfnp for small-batch-large-n; reduce wasted pipeline on full-fallback shapes.

Dropped per-iteration R accumulation: R=triu(Q^T A) recovered from the verify projection (saves one n^3 GEMM/iter). CholeskyQR iters 4->3 (borderline matrices needing more fall back to geqrf, caught by verify). Factor verify uses lower-tri leakage of Q^T A. Geomean 69822us vs baseline 111776 = 1.60x. All 22 tests + 3 guards PASS. CholeskyQR core was 64% of time; now reduced. Per-shape improved across the board incl n2048 (151849) n4096 (183192). Next bottleneck: still CholeskyQR core (gram+chol+trsm) and getrfnp on small-batch-large-n.

Shape-based (batch,n) algorithm selection: route tiny-n (n<64) and small-batch-large-n (n>1280 & b<48) to torch.geqrf; CholeskyQR otherwise. Both paths fully correct for all conditioning so this is size-based algorithm selection (cuSOLVER-style), not the forbidden conditioning dispatch. Geomean 55244us vs baseline 111776 = 2.02x. All 22 tests + 3 guards PASS. Recovered shapes 0/5/6 (tiny+small-batch-large-n) to ~1.0x. Remaining losses: shape9 rankdef b640-n512 (0.91x) and shape11 nearrank n1024 (0.82x) -- large-batch fully-ill-conditioned that route to CholeskyPath shape-wise then fall back per-matrix to geqrf, wasting CholeskyQR+verify. Next: cheaper fallback for fully-ill large-batch.

Removed the per-iteration cholesky_ex info .any() sync + emergency-shift retry from CholeskyQR (forced a GPU->CPU sync each iter). Non-PD shifted Gram now produces NaN, caught per-matrix by verify -> geqrf fallback (correct on merits). Cut dominant-shape CholeskyQR ~28% (shape3 169375->147387us). Geomean 51694us vs baseline 111776 = 2.16x. All 22 tests + 3 guards PASS. Next: getrfnp panel kernel (now larger share) and the rankdef/nearrank wasted-CholeskyQR (shapes 9,11 at ~0.9x).

First CholeskyQR iteration in TF32 (conditioning only; cond reduction doesn't need full precision), iterations 2-3 FP32 (orthonormality the verify checks). Verify+geqrf fallback catches any matrix TF32+FP32 can't orthogonalize. Geomean 51077us vs baseline 111776 = 2.19x. Shape3 147387->133290, shape4 94369->89846. All 22 tests + 3 guards PASS. Note: prototype predicted ~2.24x; investigating the fp32_precision toggle overhead. Next: getrfnp panel kernel still ~25%; rankdef/nearrank wasted CholeskyQR.

Shared-memory getrfnp panel kernel: stage active panel rows on-chip (col-major smem), factor entirely in smem (fused scale+rank-1 update, mirroring global kernel to avoid a large-batch race), avoiding global-memory round-trips; ~40% faster getrfnp for fitting n (n=512: 34->20ms). Global-memory kernel fallback when panel exceeds 99KB (early n>=1024 panels). Geomean 48670us vs baseline 111776 = 2.30x. Shape3 133290->119790. All 22 tests + 3 guards PASS.

Adaptive getrfnp panel width nb=min(48,24750//(n+1)): largest panel fitting the on-chip smem kernel (nb=48 for n<=512, 24 for n=1024); fewer trailing TRSM/GEMM launches. Geomean 48185us vs baseline 111776 = 2.32x. Shape3 119790->116371. All 22 tests + 3 guards PASS. Bottleneck now: CholeskyQR core ~45% (gram+chol+trsm x3, TRSM dominant) and the ~20-matrix geqrf fallback on borderline-dense (~31ms, refine costs more than it saves so accepted). Newton-Schulz orthogonalization tested but not competitive (slow convergence at cond~100).

CholeskyQR + orhr_col path reached 2.32x geomean (48184.6us vs baseline 111776us), HEAD=9dab86bf, all 22 tests + differential + invariance + off-grid guards PASS. WHAT WORKED: (1) CholeskyQR3 (1 TF32-conditioning iter + 2 FP32 refine iters) then orhr_col reconstruction via a custom CUDA modified-LU getrfnp (shared-memory panel kernel, adaptive panel width nb=min(48,24750/(n+1)), batched-GEMM trailing update) -- this kills the baseline's 74% scalar-panel bottleneck. (2) R=triu(Q^T A) recovered free from the verify (no per-iter R-accumulation GEMM). (3) No per-iteration cholesky_ex sync (NaN from non-PD shifted Gram caught by verify). (4) Per-matrix verify in the EXACT checker scaled-L1 metrics (orth ||Q^TQ-I||/(eps*n), factor=lower-tri leakage of Q^T A) with geqrf fallback -- correct-on-merits, passes invariance+off-grid guards, NO content-dispatch. (5) Shape-based algorithm selection: route tiny-n (n<64) and small-batch-large-n (n>1280 & batch<48) to geqrf (both paths fully correct; cuSOLVER-style size selection, not conditioning dispatch). WHAT DIDN'T: adaptive/refine-failures iteration (sync overhead exceeds geqrf-on-borderline savings); Newton-Schulz orthogonalization (slow convergence at cond~100); Newton-GEMM TRSM replacement (n^3 GEMM costlier than TRSM); shift tuning (fallback count insensitive); >1 TF32 iter (too many fallbacks). REMAINING COSTS (all fundamental): CholeskyQR core ~45% (TRSM-bound, inherently sequential, no tensor-core path); geqrf fallback on genuinely-ill matrices in mixed/rankdef/nearrank shapes (cond 1e5-1e31, no faster fully-robust method -- 'cost of accurate path is part of the score'); ~20-matrix borderline-dense geqrf fallback ~27% of dominant shape (refine costs more). SUGGESTIONS FOR NEXT BRIEF: (a) a faster batched Householder QR for the ILL-conditioned fallback path (worker-0's blocked-Householder could replace torch.geqrf there) would directly speed shapes 7/9/10/11 (the n=512 b640 ill shapes, each ~0.4-1.0s); (b) a custom fused batched SYRK+POTRF+TRSM (CholeskyQR iteration) to cut the 45% core; (c) combine with worker-2's on-chip small-n path for the tiny shapes I route to geqrf. NSYS NOTE: nsys cannot trace eval.py's multiprocessing-spawn child, so kernel-level profiles are empty; I profiled via component wall-time timing instead (documented in iteration logs).

Your CholeskyQR lane is locally physics-bound to lose (no usable tensor cores on sm_120, reconstruction >= factorization), and n=2048/4096 are confirmed unfixable in both lanes — so pivot to a DISTINCT, locally-winnable target on the GLOBAL BEST (parent 66be4189, 15.84x). FP32, all 22 tests + 3 guards green; confirm shapes 0-1 drop and nothing else regresses.

Lean small-n entry path per brief: preallocate (H,tau) + qr_into launcher (no alloc/contiguous inside extension), minimal dispatch. Result: NO improvement (shape0 34.97->34.99us, shape1 319.59->319.43us, geomean 7088->7072 = noise). RIGOROUS FINDING contradicting the brief premise: tiny shapes are GPU launch/execution-bound, NOT host-bound. Evidence: (1) CUDA-event GPU time == wall time == 34.8us for n=32 (so host work is fully hidden); (2) qr_noop (alloc+contiguous, no kernel launch) = 3.3us; (3) a trivial custom kernel same launch config (grid=20,block=32) = 3.9us, vs qr_pack = 34.8us -> the ~31us is qr_pack KERNEL EXECUTION; (4) preallocate+qr_into = identical 34.8us. So there is no ~25us host overhead to strip; the cost is the kernel exec (kernel math, forbidden here) and the tiny-grid launch latency. All 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN. geomean 7072us.

Brief 1 (micro, host/launch overhead on tiny shapes) EXHAUSTED with a clear negative result: the brief's premise is empirically false on this host. I implemented the brief literally (commit a1106037, on global-best 66be4189): for n in {32,176} preallocate (H,tau) in Python and call a new qr_into launcher that does NO allocation and NO .contiguous() inside the extension; minimal single dispatch (one shape lookup, gate once). It validated (all 22 tests + kernelguard + 3 guards CLEAN) but yielded NO speedup: shape0 34.97->34.99us, shape1 319.59->319.43us, geomean 7088->7072us (all within tiny-shape noise). ROOT CAUSE (rigorously measured): the tiny shapes are GPU launch/EXECUTION-bound, not host/pybind/alloc-bound. Evidence: (a) CUDA-event GPU-only time == wall time == 34.8us for n=32, so ALL host work is already hidden behind the launch; (b) the alloc+contiguous (qr_noop, no kernel) is only 3.3us; (c) a TRIVIAL custom kernel with the identical launch config (grid=20, block=32, via load_inline) is 3.9us, whereas qr_pack_kernel<32,1> is 34.8us -- so the ~31us is the KERNEL'S OWN EXECUTION (its 32 sequential Householder steps with per-step __syncwarp), which is kernel math explicitly out of this brief's scope; (d) M-packing sweep showed M=1 (current) is already optimal (M=2 is 84us, worse). So there is no ~25us host overhead to strip -- worker 2's earlier '~25us is PyTorch/pybind/alloc' estimate does not hold under CUDA-event isolation. RECOMMENDATION: speeding shapes 0/1 requires reducing the small-n kernel's execution/sync latency (fewer __syncwarp, fused trailing update, or a different reduction) -- that is KERNEL MATH in worker 2's lane, needs a kernel-rewrite brief, not a host-overhead micro-brief. My commit is geomean-neutral (faithful brief impl + the qr_into launcher as clean infra); it can be kept or reverted with no perf impact -- if minimal-diff is preferred for the PR, revert it. The nsys profile cannot trace eval.py's multiprocessing-spawn child (kernel-level capture empty); I used CUDA-event isolation instead, which is the decisive measurement here. No further host-side headroom on this lane.

Brief 2 done: ONE solid win (n=32) + a rigorous negative on n=176 (PRIMARY). Commit 2b1128e2 on global-best 66be4189. NET: geomean 7088->6650us = ~16.85x vs baseline (was 15.84x); all 22 tests + kernelguard + 3 guards CLEAN. NEGATIVE (n=176, PRIMARY, stays 317us): I tried 8+ variants -- full 2-sync rewrite, 4-sync (A+B fuse), 3-sync reflector-fuse, TPC sweep {2,4,5}, shuffle-only-norm, syncwarp-reflector, vsh register-cache -- EVERY ONE REGRESSED (to 409-619us). Root causes, measured: (1) on sm_120 the SUB-WARP MASKED primitives __shfl_xor_sync(colmask,..) and __syncwarp(colmask) are SLOW -- isolating just the norm-reduction-via-shuffle (else identical baseline, same 5 syncs) regressed 317->409us, so shuffle is the regressor, not the barrier count; (2) barriers are NOT the practical bottleneck: at benchmark batch=40 the kernel is CTA-STARVED (40 CTAs over 188 SMs) so the barrier-limited occupancy (ncu: 45.8%, Block Limit Barriers=24) is moot -- there are no extra CTAs to fill even with fewer barriers; (3) decomposition: reflector phase=132us (42%, serial-owner-bound -- only the column-k owner's 4 threads hold column k, so v-build can't be parallelized) + trailing update=186us (58%, shared-vsh bandwidth bound, ncu L1/TEX=52.8%); (4) register pressure RPT=44 caps occupancy and can't be cut (TPC>4 -> >1024 threads for n=176). The blocked path (W0) at n=176 is 1117us (3.5x slower), so the smem coop kernel is correctly chosen. CONCLUSION: n=176 coop<176,4> is at a local optimum for one-CTA-per-matrix; beating it needs either a 2-level/GEMM scheme that fills the GPU (structurally W0's blocked lane, which loses at n=176) or a non-warp-primitive way to cut the serial reflector latency -- neither is a micro-tweak.
